question: Explain the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM), its assumptions and its limitations.
sources: Sharpe, W. F. (1964), 'Capital Asset Prices: A Theory of Market Equilibrium under Conditions of Risk', Journal of Finance

points.label: Meaning and relationship
points.description: CAPM states that expected return equals the risk-free rate plus beta times the market risk premium; only systematic risk, measured by beta, is rewarded, and the relationship is shown by the security market line.
points.basis: Sharpe (1964): equilibrium relationship between expected return and systematic risk

points.label: Assumptions about investors
points.description: Investors are rational and risk-averse, choose portfolios on expected return and variance, have the same expectations and a single holding period.

points.label: Assumptions about markets
points.description: Markets are perfect: no taxes or transaction costs, information is freely available, assets are divisible, and investors can borrow and lend without limit at the risk-free rate.

points.label: Estimation problems
points.description: Beta is estimated from past data and may not be stable; the true market portfolio cannot be observed and the choice of risk-free rate and market premium affects results.
points.basis: Roll (1977) critique and general CAPM estimation limits

points.label: Other limitations
points.description: The assumptions are unrealistic, it is a single-factor, single-period model, and empirical tests show that factors other than beta (such as size and value) also explain returns.
points.basis: Empirical tests of CAPM, for example Fama and French (1992)
